Protectionism

/pruh-TEK-shuh-niz-uhm/ - the stress falls on TEK · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Protectionism means the policy of shielding a country's own industries from foreign competition, as with import taxes.

The island's protectionism begins at the dairy case: a stiff duty doubles the price of every imported cheese so the local creamery can match it.

Worked Example

In the 1950s the republic wrapped its infant car industry in protectionism: foreign sedans paid half their value at the docks, buyers waited years for the homely domestic model — and the factory, shielded from every rival, saw no reason to improve.

Protectionism is a policy word and often an accusation: it bundles duties, quotas, and licensing walls into a single doctrine of shelter. Its defenders say jobs; its critics say cosseted industries and pricier goods — note how the -ism turns a practice into a program.

How Protectionism Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

nativism

nativism: favors the native-born; protectionism favors home industry

autarky

autarky: the sealed extreme — needing no imports at all

Antonyms

free trade

free trade: borders open to goods, with no duties in the way

openness

openness: the general welcome protectionism walls off

How Strong Is It? — favoritism → protectionism → autarky

favoritism vs. protectionism

favoritism vs. protectionism: Favoritism is the milder lean — a thumb on the scale for local firms here and there; protectionism builds the lean into law, with duties at every port.

autarky vs. protectionism

autarky vs. protectionism: Autarky goes further than protectionism: protectionism taxes what crosses the border, while autarky tries to need nothing from across it at all.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of protectionism.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pro-

Prefix — pro-: in front

Root — tect

Root — tect: to cover (Latin tegere)

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: act of

Suffix — -ism

Suffix — -ism: policy, doctrine

Put it together

Put it together: Pro- (in front) + tect (to cover, Latin tegere) + -ion (act of) + -ism (policy) = the policy of covering in front — a shield held up before home industries. The -ism turns the shield into a doctrine.

Use the root in a new word: detect

Use the root in a new word: detect: New smoke sensors can detect a smoldering wire long before any flame shows.

Root Check

Word Choice

political / economic

Protectionism is policy vocabulary — and often an accusation — for sheltering home industries behind duties and quotas (you will meet tariff in this unit's reference list). Its opposite number is free trade. For a turning-inward that goes beyond commerce, isolationism is the broader word.
